title: CKA Week 5 Challenge - Services, DNS, Ingress, NetworkPolicy
description: End-of-week challenge for networking: every Service type, DNS verification from pods, host and path Ingress with TLS, a Gateway/HTTPRoute pair, and NetworkPolicies verified by real traffic.
scenario: Week 5 in one lab. An ingress-nginx controller and the Gateway API CRDs are pre-installed; two namespaces hold the workloads. NetworkPolicy tasks are graded by live traffic - denied pods must fail, allowed pods must succeed.
symptoms: ns apps holds web-a (nginx) and web-b (httpd) behind different host rules
ns secure holds protected + client + client2: the policy story is verified with wget, not with kubectl get
Ingress checks use real curl through the controller NodePort, exactly like debugging in the exam
mission: Wire up all Service types, prove DNS, publish two virtual hosts with TLS through Ingress, create a Gateway API route, and lock down ns secure with default-deny plus surgical allow rules.

hints.title: Behavior beats objects
hints.content: Tasks 6-8 and 9-11 check LIVE traffic through the ingress controller and NetworkPolicy engine. If curl/wget fails, debug with kubectl get endpoints, kubectl describe ingress and the controller logs - the week 7 order.

hints.title: NodePort discovery
hints.content: The controller publishes 80/443 as NodePorts on the single node (k3s-server). Grab them with jsonpath as shown in the solutions, then curl with a Host header.

hints.title: NetworkPolicy AND/OR semantics
hints.content: Selectors inside ONE from entry are AND; separate entries are OR. Write the DNS egress rule first whenever you write egress rules, or nslookup dies too.

hints.title: Gateway API
hints.content: The CRDs and a GatewayClass named cka-gc are pre-installed. Create a Gateway (listener on :80) and an HTTPRoute attaching to it; existence and class are checked, no controller implements it.

acceptance_criteria.description: Service web-a-svc (ClusterIP 80) in apps has ready endpoints
Service web-a-np in apps is a NodePort
Headless Service web-a-headless in apps (clusterIP: None)
ExternalName Service external-db points to db.example.com
Cluster DNS resolves web-a-svc.apps.svc.cluster.local from a pod
Ingress app-ingress routes app.example.com to web-a-svc (verified with curl)
Second virtual host api.example.com routes to web-b-svc (curl shows the httpd page)
TLS ingress: secret app-tls serves https for app.example.com (curl -k)
NetworkPolicy default-deny in secure: client CANNOT reach protected (live traffic)
Allow rule: client2 (label access=allowed) CAN reach protected
DNS egress preserved: client can still resolve kubernetes.default
Gateway API: a Gateway and an HTTPRoute exist (class cka-gc)
